title: Washington Post Reports Trump Allies Drafted Conditional Day-One Insurrection Act Plans
description_short: The Washington Post reported in November 2023 that Trump allies were drafting conditional day-one plans to invoke the Insurrection Act against civil demonstrations.
description_medium: On Nov. 6, 2023, The Washington Post reported that Trump associates were drafting plans to potentially invoke the Insurrection Act on the first day of a possible second term, allowing military deployment against civil demonstrations. The report attributes planning to his associates and Project 2025; it does not establish a public promise by Trump, an adopted policy, or Pentagon preparations.
description_long:
On Nov. 6, 2023, The Washington Post reported that Donald Trump’s associates were drafting plans to potentially invoke the Insurrection Act on the first day of a possible second term, allowing military deployment against civil demonstrations. The article attributed the plans to Trump allies and described Project 2025 as developing a plan, including draft executive orders, for domestic military deployment under the Act. It reported that internal communications identified the proposal as an immediate priority. The story also explained that the Act authorizes a president to deploy the military for domestic law enforcement.

The account describes conditional planning, not an adopted campaign policy or an order. It does not establish that Trump publicly promised to invoke the Act, that the Act was invoked, or that troops were deployed. The supplied record’s additional claims about mass deportation, protest suppression as a purpose, and Pentagon officials or military lawyers preparing for possible unlawful orders are not established by this report and are omitted.

quotes: Donald Trump and his allies have begun mapping out specific plans for using the federal government to punish critics and opponents should he win a second term, with the former president naming individuals he wants to investigate or prosecute and his associates drafting plans to potentially invoke the Insurrection Act on his first day in office to allow him to deploy the military against civil demonstrations.

Dubbed “Project 2025,” the group is developing a plan, to include draft executive orders, that would deploy the military domestically under the Insurrection Act, according to a person involved in those conversations and internal communications reviewed by The Washington Post. The law, last updated in 1871, authorizes the president to deploy the military for domestic law enforcement.
The proposal was identified in internal discussions as an immediate priority, the communications showed.
supports: The Nov. 6, 2023 report attributes conditional first-day Insurrection Act planning to Trump’s associates if he won a second term.
The report says the contemplated deployment was against civil demonstrations.
The report describes Project 2025 developing draft executive orders for domestic military deployment and says internal communications called the proposal an immediate priority.
limitations: The report does not establish that Trump himself publicly promised to invoke the Act, that the plan became adopted campaign policy, or that an order, invocation, or deployment occurred.
The report does not support the staged claims that the purpose was mass deportation or protest suppression, or that Pentagon officials or military lawyers prepared for possible unlawful orders.
